sections.h2: Which Floyd County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
In Floyd County one office sets values and another collects, and both work out of Rome. The Tax Commissioner is in the Floyd County Historic Courthouse at 5 Government Plaza, Suite 109, Rome, GA 30161, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 26, Rome, GA 30162. For property tax, call (706) 291-5146 or (706) 291-5148 on weekdays between eight and five.

The assessors appraise every real and personal property account in the county and in Rome itself. The county notes that the Assessor's Office relocated to the former Law Enforcement Center at 5 Government Plaza, and the tax site lists (706) 291-5143 for the assessor.

Tax for the City of Rome is on the county bill. The three rate-setters are the Floyd County Board of Commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Floyd County Board of Education.

sections.h2: What should I know about selling a house in Rome and Floyd County?
sections.html:
Rome is built among three rivers, the Etowah, the Oostanaula and the Coosa, and the city's own water documents tie them to its early trading history. Floyd measures 509.81 land square miles, the biggest of the three counties in the Bureau's side-by-side table with Fayette and Fannin, and counted 193.4 people per square mile in 2020.

Health care is a large employer here. The Bureau lists 2022 health care and social assistance receipts of $1,653,925 thousand for Floyd, topping Fayette's total although Fayette has more residents.

A house in town and a house outside it go through the same assessors but can carry different bills, since the city rate applies only inside Rome. Ask which taxing districts cover your parcel.

sections.h2: Who lives in Floyd County and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
The mid-2025 estimate is 101,378 residents, a 2.8 percent rise over the 98,589 counted as the 2020 base. Renters hold a large slice: owners occupy 63.6 percent of homes, the lowest share in the three-county table.

  • Typical owned home, valued at $217,900 (survey years 2020 to 2024).
  • Median gross rent: $1,014 a month.
  • Housing units in 2025: 41,737 and 36,856 households.
  • Median household income: $65,565.
  • Persons in poverty: 14.9 percent.
  • Four-year degree holders among adults 25 and up: 25.9 percent.
  • Average trip to work: 23.3 minutes, shortest of the three.
  • Building permits in 2025: 330.

Values near $218,000 and rents just over $1,000 mean the tax questions below matter to landlords and families selling a parent's house as much as to owner-occupants.

sections.h2: When is Floyd County property tax due?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner's site puts the usual due date at November 15, with real and personal property statements mailed by September 1.

  • Interest builds monthly once the date passes, and a penalty of up to 20 percent can be added.
  • Mobile homes get statements by February 1 and owe by April 1; a late payer faces a 10 percent penalty and possibly a citation.
  • For mailed checks the office honors a postmark from the U.S. Postal Service and rejects metered ones.
  • The office mails to the owner and never to the lender, so pass your copy along if a servicer pays your tax.
  • Once taxes sit unpaid past 90 days, a tax fifa can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, a public record that credit bureaus may pick up.

The Tax Commissioner's site announced that Floyd County would hold 2026 tax sales tentatively starting May 5, 2026, with listings posted on the website. That date has passed, so ask the office when the next sale schedule is published.

sections.h2: How do I challenge my Floyd County value?
sections.html:
Put your appeal in writing to the Floyd County Board of Assessors, 5 Government Plaza, Rome, GA 30161, inside 45 days of the notice date. One that arrives or is postmarked after the stated deadline does not count.

Steps after a Floyd County notice of assessment (source: Board of Assessors)
StepWhat happensTime limit
Written appealSent to the Board of Assessors with your opinion of value45 days from the notice date
Staff reviewValue is raised, lowered or left aloneIf changed, 30 days to appeal the new value
Board of EqualizationThree members appointed by the Grand Jury for three-year terms hear itAutomatic if no change is made
Superior CourtEither side can continue after the board's decisionWritten notice to the Board of Assessors

Arbitration is available instead of the Board of Equalization, at the owner's option when the appeal is filed. Grounds are taxability, uniformity, value and denial of homestead. The estimated tax on the notice cannot be the basis. Include the map reference from your notice, the filing method you choose, your estimate of value, a short reason and a daytime phone number.

sections.h2: What homestead and special programs does Floyd County offer?
sections.html:
Local Floyd exemptions replace the state ones wherever the local amount is bigger. The tax site lists regular, veterans and elderly homestead exemptions, with an extra exemption at age 62. File at the Tax Assessor's Office, with your warranty deed if the house is your first.

A form can arrive any month, yet an application received after April 1 starts the benefit a year later. After approval it renews on its own until the residence, owner or exemption type changes.

  • Homeowners 62 or older whose gross household income is $15,000 or less can defer tax on part or all of the homestead, with repayment due at a change of ownership or when the balance reaches 85 percent of market value.
  • Farm property in bona fide use is assessed at 30 percent rather than 40, and conservation use programs ask for a covenant of at least 10 years.
  • Timber still standing escapes tax until cut or sold.
  • Manufacturers may qualify for freeport exemption, with applications between January 1 and April 1.

Before signing a contract on land under such a covenant, ask the assessors what the sale does to it.

sections.h2: What should a Floyd County seller do about the tax bill?
sections.html:
Request the balance from the Tax Commissioner and write the year's split into the contract. Georgia values property as of January 1 each year, and bills are generally mailed by September 1, so a spring sale can close before the year's bill exists.

The Floyd County Clerk of Superior Court, not the tax office, collects intangible tax on a long-term mortgage, and warranty deed copies come from its deed room at 3 Government Plaza. A mobile home seller should confirm the April 1 tax and decal are current.

Assessment notices are also tied to site visits. Floyd's assessors must notify owners before inspecting, under O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1, and visits follow a sale or purchase, new construction, an active building permit, a return, an appeal or an exemption application. Appraisers drive marked county vehicles and carry identification.

faqs.q: When are Floyd County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15 is the usual date for real estate and business personal property. Mobile homes fall due April 1, and real property statements generally go out by September 1.

faqs.q: What is the Floyd County appeal window?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date, in writing, to the Board of Assessors at 5 Government Plaza, Rome. A late one is rejected.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Floyd County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest accrues monthly after November 15 and a penalty of up to 20 percent may follow. Continued nonpayment can bring a lien and further collection steps.

faqs.q: Does the City of Rome send its own property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Taxes for the City of Rome are included on the Floyd County tax bill. The county commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Board of Education each set their own rate.

faqs.q: Can older Floyd County homeowners postpone paying property tax?
faqs.a: Some can. A homestead owner aged 62 or more with gross household income of $15,000 or less may defer part or all of the tax, and the deferral ends at a transfer of ownership or when deferred tax plus interest hits 85 percent of fair market value.
